conviction_note: Small positive lean (p_up 54 on a 4.0% abs move gives +0.32): a stock sold down 23% from its 13 Oct high on the unwind of spot tanker rates heads into a mostly time-chartered quarter that peers say was flat versus Q2, a dividend raise management pre-signalled, and a call that can quote record Q4 profit-share earnings. Against that, the sector tape (VLCC rates -64% from peak by 13 Nov) still drives the stock, TEN shrugged its Q2 beat (+0.9%) and reportedly sold its Q1 beat, and the bar is disputed ($1.90 vs $3.55). The findings sum to +0.6 and the scaled number is +0.32. They differ because the findings carry a dividend item and a Q4 item at their own size, while p_up stays near 50 because of the bar dispute and the reaction history.

findings.finding: Teekay Tankers trades the same Suezmax and Aframax/LR2 classes as TEN's core fleet. Its Q3 2026 spot rates were slightly below Q2 (Suezmax $106,437 vs $109,171/day, -2.5%; Aframax/LR2 $67,552 vs $74,149, -8.9%), while its time-charter-out rates rose (Suezmax $60,470 vs $57,773; Aframax $41,539 vs $37,043). TEN had 84% of its fleet on time charter in Q2 and 12% of days in spot, so its Q3 TCE should be roughly flat to slightly up on Q2's $46,100/day. That points to adjusted EPS near Q2's $3.14, slightly under the disputed $3.55 bar, rather than a large beat.
findings.link: Same vessel classes (Suezmax, Aframax/LR2) and the same spot and time-charter markets; TEN's profit-share and spot vessels index to these rates. No shared customers stated.

findings.finding: TEN's 2026-09-28 release says the sale of the 2003-built Panamax Andes yields a $4.6M capital gain 'to be recorded in Q3 2026' (about $0.15/share). The two 2006-built Suezmaxes Alaska and Archangel, sold in August for about $100M net, may add a further gain in Q3 or Q4 that the company has never quantified. So GAAP EPS will likely print above every consensus figure, while the street measures on adjusted EPS (as with Q2: GAAP $4.40 vs adjusted $3.14).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 carried a $37.9M gain (headline $4.40 vs $2.50 estimate) and the stock moved +0.88% on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: The gains are public. Only a headline-reading algorithm would react, and Q2 showed little such reaction. The cash goes into the newbuild programme (path to dividend capacity) but has no stated path to the guide.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-09-10) CEO Nikolas Tsakos said the dividend is announced after the November strategy meeting and that he was 'looking forward for an increase of that'. The Q2 release states the first semi-annual 2027 dividend 'will be announced in November 2026'. The last payment was $1.00 per share (July 2026), so the Q3 release on 19 Nov is the likely venue for a raise above $1.00.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In May 2026 the semi-annual dividend rose from $0.50 to $1.00 alongside a 37% Q1 beat, and the stock reportedly fell about 4-5% (unverified). The November 2025 declaration was paired with the Q3 2025 print; no verified reaction was found.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction (an increase) was pre-signalled, so it is largely priced. The size is not: a raise to $1.25 vs $1.50+ is unknown. A 23% drawdown from the October high and a 2.3% trailing yield on $1.00 semi-annual suggest the market is not paying for a large raise. If it were, the stock would not have fallen in step with spot rates while TEN's earnings are 84% time-chartered. The size is held small because the raise lands inside what management already signalled, and a token raise would disappoint.
findings.independence: Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/390858/ten-ltd-reports-profits-for-the-first-half-and-second-quarter-of-2026) states the November dividend announcement. That is the same company, a separate document.

findings.finding: Into the print TEN is down 17.2% over 20 sessions and 23.1% from its 13 Oct high of $56.40, including -8.6% over the last three sessions to $43.35. Spot is 31% below the $62.50 mean analyst target, and Alliance Global raised its target to $65 on 28 Oct. The market has sold the spot-rate unwind hard, even though TEN's earnings are 84% time-chartered and carry $3.5-3.6B of contracted revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After Q2 (10 Sep) the stock rose from $44.71 to $52.81 over five sessions as the market re-rated contracted earnings. That move came during a rising rate market, so it is not a clean comparison.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were pricing TEN as a charter-backed fleet, the drawdown would be smaller than spot-heavy peers'. Instead TEN fell 23% from its high, about the same as INSW's 21% from its own high, although TEN has less spot exposure. A quarter and call that stress backlog could close part of that gap. The size is small because the sector tape is still falling (the last three sessions alone took -8.6%).
findings.independence: Targets: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ten/forecast/ (2026-10-28). Same-direction context: INSW 21% off its high into its print (https://finviz.com/news/417364/international-seaways-beats-handily-but-the-story-is-a-q4-rate-spike-that-dwarfs-a-flat-q3).

findings.finding: VLCC Gulf-China rates fell 64%, from WS 841 on 8 Oct to WS 308 on 13 Nov. Brokers attribute the fall to Gulf exports returning toward prewar levels and the geopolitical risk premium unwinding, with oil down about 20% in November on Iran de-escalation hopes. TEN's spot and profit-share vessels (37% of the fleet) are exposed to this in Q4 and Q1, and the tanker tape, not the quarter, has driven the stock (-8.1% on 2 Nov, -8.6% over 16-18 Nov).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no print-day precedent. On ordinary days of falling rates TEN moved -3% to -8% in November (stockanalysis history).
findings.why_not_priced: This is largely priced: it is the reason for the drawdown. It is filed because the print day sits inside a falling sector tape, and a further leg down in rates or de-escalation news on 19 Nov would swamp company news. It is a macro-to-company proxy: TEN has not commented on November rates.
findings.independence: Teekay's 11 Nov release says 'freight markets have moderated from recent peak levels' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001419945/000141994526000070/tnkq3-26erdocument.htm). Atlantic tanker earnings falling (https://cyprusshippingnews.com/2026/11/12/atlantic-tanker-earnings-fall-faster-than-gulf-earnings/).

lessons_applied: Rule 2 (one-offs): the vessel-sale gain finding, which has no path to the guide, was cut from +0.3 to +0.1.

Rule 6 (bar disputed: $1.90 vs $3.55) and rule 1 (this name sold or shrugged its last two beats): the pre-signalled dividend raise lands inside what management already guided, so it was cut from +0.8 to +0.5. p_up was cut from 55 to 54.
